# network-tools

> network-tools (backend name: Network-Tools) is a free, open-source, self-hosted domain monitor. It checks DNS, email authentication and TLS for many domains on a schedule, stores a history of every check run, and sends email alerts only when something gets worse, is fixed, or changes. It runs as a Docker image with PostgreSQL, typically deployed with Coolify. Login uses passkeys or one-time magic links; there are no passwords. The backend UI is in German; the documentation is in English.

## Checks

- MX: records, null MX (RFC 7505), A/AAAA of MX hosts, MX pointing to an IP address or CNAME
- A / AAAA: domain and www (or custom web hosts), missing IPv6, private or reserved addresses
- PTR: reverse DNS of MX and outgoing mail server IPs, forward-confirmed reverse DNS (FCrDNS)
- SPF: duplicate records, +all / ?all, recursive counter for the 10 DNS lookup limit including redirect, void lookup limit of 2
- DKIM: known selectors per provider (Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, Mailchimp, SendGrid, Mailjet, Brevo, HubSpot, Zoho, Mailgun, IONOS, Mailcow) plus custom selectors; AWS SES Easy DKIM tokens (CNAME to *.dkim.amazonses.com) rated as a group: one active key is OK, reserve tokens with empty p= are info; error below 1024-bit RSA, warning below 2048-bit
- DMARC: p, sp, pct, rua, authorization record for external report receivers
- MTA-STS: TXT record, HTTPS policy, mode, max_age, every MX host covered by the policy
- TLS-RPT: record and report targets; warning if MTA-STS is active without TLS-RPT
- BIMI: record, SVG Tiny PS logo up to 32 KB, DMARC enforcement requirement, VMC/CMC
- DNSSEC: DS at the parent, DNSKEY, DS matched to DNSKEY by key tag, RRSIG expiry, validation via the AD flag, SERVFAIL detection, deprecated algorithms
- Name servers (NS/SOA): delegation and glue read directly from a parent-zone (registry) server, NXDOMAIN at the registry, missing glue for in-domain name servers; each authoritative server queried directly with response times; lame delegation, SOA serial consistency (info only for multi-provider setups), NS list vs delegation, same /24 network, SOA timer sanity
- CAA: allowed CAs (issue/issuewild), lookup climbs to parent names, issue ";" warning, unknown critical tags, iodef
- TLS certificate (HTTPS): trust, host name, expiry for domain, www and mta-sts; outdated TLS versions
- TLS certificate (SMTP STARTTLS, optional, needs outgoing port 25): availability, trust, host name, expiry
- HTTP → HTTPS / HSTS: redirect chain from http:// to https:// (up to 6 hops), Strict-Transport-Security max-age (recommended ≥ 1 year), includeSubDomains, preload readiness
- DANE (TLSA): _25._tcp TLSA of every MX host, DNSSEC validation, usage 3 1 1 / 2 1 1 recommended, match against the STARTTLS certificate when port 25 is available
- Domain expiry: RDAP via IANA bootstrap; registries without RDAP expiry (e.g. DENIC for .de) are reported as info
- Blacklists: free RBLs (SpamCop, PSBL, Mailspike, UCEPROTECT Level 1, SURBL, URIBL; Barracuda optional); Spamhaus ZEN and DBL only via Spamhaus DQS with your own key

## Tools

- Tools (on demand, nothing stored): MX lookup with priority; IP (A/AAAA at every authoritative name server and at ten public resolvers: Google, Cloudflare, Quad9, Cisco OpenDNS, AdGuard, CleanBrowsing, Control D, Comodo, Lumen/Level 3, Yandex); name servers with SOA serial; SOA fields; CNAME chain; TXT records with type; CAA with inheritance
- Mail security tools: SPF, DMARC, DKIM (known selectors per provider or custom), MTA-STS, TLS-RPT, DANE for any domain, same rules as the monitoring
- Reverse DNS: PTR for an IP or all IPs of a host name, with FCrDNS
- Troubleshooting: trace from the root servers (where resolution breaks), DNSSEC signatures (RRSIG) with validity, DS at the parent matched against the DNSKEYs

- AI copilot (optional): AI models configured in the backend (Anthropic Claude via the official SDK, OpenAI, Google Gemini, OpenRouter, OpenAI-compatible such as Ollama or Mistral; API keys encrypted); recommendations per finding or for all findings, answers cached 7 days; results are sent to the provider only on request
- Export for AI chat: instructions plus the full current state as text or Markdown file for pasting into any AI chat

## Alerts

- Mail on: worse status, fixed problem (optional), other status change, configuration change with the same status (different records)
- Never on: timeouts or resolver problems ("not checkable")
- IP changes of A/AAAA and PTR are only logged unless enabled per domain
- Recipients: global + per customer + per domain; per customer a mail level (all changes, from info, from warning, errors only, none)
- Default thresholds: certificate warning 21 days, error 7 days; domain warning 30 days, error 7 days
- Intervals per domain: hourly, 3, 6, 12 hours or daily; scheduler runs every 5 minutes; logs kept 180 days by default
